name: Libsyn
tagline: Podcast hosting, distribution, analytics, advertising, and monetization

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.limits: Exact upload and feature caps are not disclosed on the public pricing page

tiers.name: Max

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; every paid plan has a 30-day trial requiring a card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only on public self-serve plans; no annual plan published
pricing.hiddenCosts: Plans meter newly uploaded audio each month; advanced professional features and enterprise service are custom-priced.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Libsyn's durable value is media pipeline, hosting, distribution, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local podcast hosting workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: recording recovery, mastering, hosting, and distribution
whyPeopleStillPay: Libsyn: People pay to avoid codec failures, upload limits, rendering surprises, lost recordings, and distribution chores.
ongoingBurden: Maintain codecs, media probing, resumable processing, storage cleanup, exports, device permissions, and performance.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

alternatives.name: Castopod
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted podcasting with analytics, distribution and monetization tools; you become the hosting company.

facts.install: Install the PHP package on a HTTPS web server with MySQL or MariaDB and cron, or use a community YunoHost package
facts.dataFormat: Podcast metadata and analytics live in MySQL or MariaDB; audio and artwork live on the server filesystem under public/media or in S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: You become the hosting company: CDN, storage, backups, updates and support, without Libsyn's managed distribution, advertising scale or operator help.
facts.setupBlocker: A PHP web host, database, HTTPS, cron, writable paths and usually SMTP must all be configured

alternatives.name: RedCircle Core
alternatives.desc: Unlimited hosting and monetization for one show; cross-promotion and free-form ad insertion still cost.

facts.install: Hosted signup and podcast import or upload
facts.dataFormat: Audio, episode metadata, RSS feed, analytics and monetization data live in RedCircle's hosted platform
facts.gapVsPaid: It is limited to one show and standard analytics, while cross-promotion, custom dynamic insertion, exports, team seats and advanced analytics require payment.

alternatives.name: RSS.com
alternatives.desc: A real free host with unlimited episodes; your analytics memory is 30 days.

facts.install: Hosted signup and podcast import or upload
facts.dataFormat: Audio files, episode metadata, public RSS feed, website and analytics live in RSS.com's hosted platform
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan remembers only 30 days of analytics, and programmatic ads, AI transcripts, multiple shows and team seats require paid tiers.

alternatives.name: Spotify for Creators
alternatives.desc: Unlimited podcast hosting for zero dollars; the landlord is Spotify.

facts.install: Hosted Spotify account signup and podcast import or upload
facts.dataFormat: Uploaded audio or video, show metadata, RSS feed and analytics live in Spotify's cloud; creators retain ownership of episode content
facts.gapVsPaid: Its strongest monetization is eligibility- and market-dependent, and the service is optimized for Spotify's ecosystem rather than host-neutral publisher control.

alternatives.name: Spreaker Free Speech
alternatives.desc: One unlimited show with distribution, six months of stats and ads; private feeds still cost.

facts.install: Hosted signup in the browser or through Spreaker Create mobile and web tools
facts.engines: Optional ad auto-optimization uses Sounder's AI-generated ad markers
facts.dataFormat: One show's audio, RSS feed, distribution settings and six months of statistics live in Spreaker's hosted platform
facts.gapVsPaid: It allows one show and six months of statistics, with no collaboration, private feeds or advanced analytics, and takes 20% of Supporters Club revenue.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Buzzsprout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Free until your episodes turn 90 days old, which is not what hosting means.

notes: Credibility row: Libsyn survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Libsyn; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + FFmpeg + React.
Primary job: Build a local podcast hosting workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large-scale rendering; distribution and podcast hosting; professional codecs, effects, and collaboration.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
